analysis:
Both changed files are offline test scripts; no production code is modified in the supplied units. scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py (head lines 107-121) adds tests that a workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev resolves to a published dev build, stamped 0.9.0-dev.branch.42. The tests expect validation and version overrides to be ignored, and non-dev environments (empty, prod, staging) to fail with "Dev branch releases publish dev only" and emit no outputs. scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py extends FakeAPI with a dev-HEAD commit lookup and a dev self-compare. It adds tests that a dev dispatch is admitted only for environment dev and only when GITHUB_SHA equals the current dev HEAD ("current dev commit"), while prod, staging and empty environments are refused. A schedule event is refused with "trusted tag push".

Security relevance is to release-signing integrity (A-011, T-034, T-054). The tests tighten fail-closed behavior on that path and encode that dev-branch dispatch never reaches the prod or staging signing identity. The behavior the tests assert lives in resolve-provider-release.sh and provider_release_resume/api.py, and neither is in this batch. The real change to the dispatch gate, the workflow permissions and which signing identity or secrets a dev publication can reach cannot be verified from these units. Integration should confirm that the implementation matches the tests. In particular, it should check that dev dispatch is gated on the dev HEAD plus the verified-commit check, that a dispatch on dev cannot select the prod environment or the signing identity, and that the head-SHA race is closed. The removed base test test_dev_validation_and_resume_source_must_be_current_reviewed_master remains unchanged. In the resolution script's tests, the base test for a dispatch on the candidate branch publishing dev still fails closed. No regression is attributable to these test-only changes.
